tagline: A ranch family's road over the mountains to the sea.
intro: North of Ojai, Highway 33 goes up Matilija Canyon into Los Padres National Forest. At Wheeler Gorge it runs through three tunnels along the foot of sharp cliffs and a boulder-strewn creek. Then it drops into the Sespe Creek watershed past the white sandstone of Piedra Blanca, and climbs out of the chaparral into Douglas fir and ponderosa pine to cross the Transverse Ranges at Pine Mountain Summit.

The Reyes family largely mapped the route, to get from their ranch on the Cuyama side down to the coast. It was called the Maricopa Highway and meant to carry trade between the San Joaquin Valley and southern California. These days it is especially popular with motorcyclists.

moments.title: Wheeler Springs
moments.text: In 1890 Wheeler Blumberg climbed into a ravine after a deer he had shot and found hot sulphur springs. The next year he opened a resort there with 14 cabins.

moments.title: Bellyache Springs
moments.text: Named, the story goes, for early travelers who arrived so thirsty they drank too much. A Forest Service version has rangers meeting here on horseback to bellyache about the job.

moments.title: Sespe Gorge
moments.text: Vertical walls on the upper Sespe Creek where rock climbers practice bouldering and rappelling. The gorge's south end is the Sespe Condor Sanctuary, closed to the public.
